blocks.task_summary: Find the time t when the particle is at rest by solving v(t) = e^(sin t) + 4 sin t = 0 for t in [0, 6].
method_path: Solve e^(sin t) + 4 sin t = 0 using GDC

evidence.basis: recognizing at rest v=0 (M1); t = 3.34692... t = 3.35 (seconds) A1; Note: Award (M1)A0 for any other solution to v=0 eg t=-0.205 or t=6.08.

blocks.task_summary: Find the acceleration when the particle changes direction by differentiating v(t) and evaluating a(t) at the t from part (a).
method_path: Recognize direction change occurs when v = 0 at t = 3.34692...
Differentiate v(t): a(t) = e^(sin t) cos t + 4 cos t

evidence.basis: recognizing particle changes direction when v=0 OR when t=3.34692... (M1); a = -4.71439... a = -4.71 (ms^-2) A2

blocks.task_summary: Find the total distance travelled by integrating the absolute value of v(t) from t = 0 to 6.
method_path: Set total distance = integral of |v(t)| from 0 to 6
Split at t = 3.34692... where v changes sign
Evaluate integral of v(t) from 0 to 3.34692... plus integral of -v(t) from 3.34692... to 6 using GDC
accepted_alternatives: Direct evaluation of integral of |v(t)| from 0 to 6 using GDC without explicit splitting

evidence.basis: distance travelled = integral_0^6 |v| dt OR split integrals (A1); = 20.7534... = 20.8 (metres) A1
